findings.detail:
The always-present sr-only live region at line 1360 announces the result once, and the visible copy inside the `role="region"` panel is marked `aria-hidden="true"` so it is "not read twice". But the visible `

` is not inside any live region — a newly mounted, non-live subtree is not auto-announced — so there was no double-read to prevent. The net effect is that a screen-reader user who misses the polite announcement (it is transient, and polite yields to other speech) or who navigates back to the "Ready to upload" region afterwards finds a heading and two download buttons with no counts at all: how many raw materials, how many identical, how many not. The one place the numbers live is permanently removed from the accessibility tree.
findings.summary: aria-hidden on the visible summary hides the result from AT permanently

findings.detail: When `readyPlan.problems` is non-empty the panel never appears and the only trace is an `'info'` log line. Every other recoverable shortfall in this same handler uses `'warning'` (the Cost & Profit note at line 959, the identical-count note at line 1009, the error summary at line 1013). The user's experience is a feature that silently does not exist; they have to open the Logs panel and scan past info lines to learn that, e.g., a required SKU column was not found. The e2e spec at `e2e/composite-ready-to-upload.spec.ts:197` has to click the logs button to see it, which is the tell.
findings.summary: "Ready to upload was not built" is logged at 'info', not 'warning'

findings.detail: `col(h)` is `COMPOSITE_UPLOAD_HEADERS.indexOf(h)` over a 73-entry array, and it is called 4 times for the fixed fields plus twice per ingredient slot (60) on every source row — ~64 scans, ~2,400 string comparisons per row. The headers are a module-level constant, so the lookup table can be built once instead of per cell. This is not a user-visible freeze at realistic composite-product counts (hundreds of rows ≈ a few ms), which is why it is `low` rather than `high`; it would move up if composite sheets reached tens of thousands of rows.
findings.summary: checkCompositeUpload does ~64 linear header lookups per row
